newsitem.title: USA: Conn. governor to decide on Whalers arena soon.
newsitem.headline: Conn. governor to decide on Whalers arena soon.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland on Tuesday said he would decide in the next three to four weeks whether the state could afford to help build a new arena for the Hartford Whalers of National Hockey League (NHL).
The Whalers have said the state would have to build a new arena, costing as much as $240 million in taxpayers' money, if it wanted the team to stay in Connecticut.
Rowland told reporters that if he decided the state could not afford a new facility for the franchise, he would probably let the team out of its lease, which runs through the 1998 season.
"If they decide to leave and if we can't afford to build a new facility, then we need to go to Plan B -- and that's to get more services and more functions in the Hartford Civic Center," he said.
Options included luring another professional hockey team, Rowland said. "Maybe not NHL, but maybe the next league down, and find 100 other things we could do at the Civic Center."
Rowland is awaiting architectural studies on a new facility.
Whalers owner Peter Karmanos has said he cannot sustain the kind of losses the team has suffered for the past two years.
The governor and Karmanos have ruled out refurbishing the Civic Center for the team.
